record.enforcement: GDI confirms goods prohibition June 29, 2025. Hun Sen reiterates the closed-land-border goods prohibition June 13, 2026 while acknowledging Thai merchandise circulating in Cambodia. This is later official policy testimony, not independent proof of continuous enforcement.
record.status_observation: Latest adopted policy assertion dated 2026-06-13; actual continuity and universal implementation not established.
record.official_rationale: Reciprocal response to Thai closure; restoration made conditional on Thai reopening.
record.uncertainty: Confirmed inforce June 29; precise introduction date and endpoint not established. Opposite-side policy overlay on EA001, not an independent physical border interval. Round11 found no direct support for an Elite politics mechanism; that code is removed. July16 selected-commodity import rules do not establish land-gate reopening. GDI announcement repeated by AKP and CamboJA is one policy lineage; nationwide implementation is not independently observed. Round14 targeted scope/continuity follow-up adds June 13, 2026 official assertion only; the roughly one-year wording is not adopted as an exact or uninterrupted physical closure duration.

followup_reviews.Research finding: Retain the included Cambodian goods-crossing prohibition as a formal policy observation. Government testimony establishes the restriction’s stated existence without proving universal physical implementation. Retain goods entry, exit and transit through Cambodian international and regional gates facing Thailand. Neither passenger closure nor sea/air prohibition is added, and no joint Thai–Cambodian all-traffic spell is assumed. Retain EA002-FU1’s 29 June 2025 confirmation with unknown onset and repeal under withheld_unknown_onset. The 13 June 2026 assertion remains later policy testimony; it does not fill the interval or turn the conditional five-hour promise into actual return. Retain Trade and protectionism / Import, export and production controls and Interstate disputes and pressure / Diplomatic disputes and retaliation, limited to the reported goods measure and the explicit condition on Thai gate restoration. Both sources are Cambodian government-agency accounts of GDI or Hun Sen statements, not two independent operational investigations. The later account acknowledges merchandise leakage, which prevents blanket enforcement certainty. Retain unlocated national frontier-gate policy scope and null coordinates. No gate-specific onset, common line or current restriction map is derived from national statements.
